subtopics.title: Ten Thousand Years of Slow, Two Centuries of Fast

questions.question: The world reached its first one billion people around:
The population explosion of the last two centuries was caused mainly by:
options: A sudden worldwide rise in birth rates
Mass migration between continents
Death rates collapsing — through food, clean water, vaccines and antibiotics — while birth rates stayed high
Warmer climates increasing harvests everywhere

questions.question: Population growth described as a J-curve means:
options: A long, almost flat stretch across the centuries, then a bend into a nearly vertical climb
Steady, straight-line growth from the beginning
Rapid early growth followed by centuries of decline
Growth that rises and falls every decade

questions.question: World population is still rising even though the growth rate has fallen since the late 1960s because:
options: Death rates are rising again
The United Nations miscounts each year
Immigration adds people to the world total
Momentum — the huge cohorts already born keep producing children even as families shrink

subtopics.title: Measuring Growth — Natural Increase and Doubling Time

questions.question: A country has 30 births and 10 deaths per thousand people per year. Its natural increase is:
options: 40 per thousand, or 4% a year
10 per thousand, or 1% a year
3 per thousand, or 0,3% a year
20 per thousand, or 2% a year

questions.question: Using the rule of 70, a population growing at 2% a year doubles in about:
options: 35 years
70 years
20 years
140 years

questions.question: Doubling time behaves like compound interest because:
options: Banks calculate both figures
Each year's increase adds people who themselves produce the next year's increase
Populations only grow in leap years
The rule of 70 was invented by economists

questions.question: Which matching of country to growth situation is correct?
options: Niger shrinking; Japan doubling in 20 years; South Africa at 4%
Niger at about 1%; Japan at 3,7%; South Africa shrinking
Niger growing at roughly 3,7%; Japan shrinking as deaths exceed births; South Africa near 1%
All three countries growing at exactly 2%

questions.question: A region is overpopulated when:
options: Its density exceeds 100 people per square kilometre
Its population exceeds the carrying capacity of its resources and technology
It has more than ten million people
Most of its people live in cities

questions.question: The Netherlands, with over 500 people per square kilometre, is NOT overpopulated because:
options: Its population is falling rapidly
Density figures for Europe are unreliable
Most Dutch people live abroad
Its fertile land, technology and strong economy support its people at a high standard of living

questions.question: Parts of the arid Sahel can be overpopulated at under 20 people per square kilometre because:
options: Rainfall is so scarce and soils so thin that even a sparse population presses beyond what the land can regenerate
The Sahel has the world's highest birth rate
Density is always highest in deserts
The region's cities are overcrowded

questions.question: Carrying capacity is not fixed. It can be RAISED by:
options: Overgrazing and deforestation
Falling water tables
Irrigation, fertiliser and improved seed, which let the same land feed more people
Soil erosion on marginal ground

questions.question: The single most reliable measure ever found for lowering birth rates is:
options: Building larger stadiums
Banning large families by law
Increasing food imports
Keeping girls in school longer — educated women marry later, earn incomes and use family planning

questions.question: Reducing infant mortality lowers birth rates because:
options: Parents stop having insurance children once child survival becomes normal
Hospitals limit family sizes
Fewer surviving children means a smaller population immediately
Vaccines reduce fertility directly

questions.question: China's one-child policy is treated as a cautionary case because it:
options: Had no effect on the birth rate at all
Was copied successfully by every other country
Cut births but left an ageing population, a shrinking workforce and a skewed sex ratio
Was only applied in rural areas

questions.question: Thailand and Kerala matter in this debate because they:
options: Achieved fertility declines comparable to China's through education, healthcare and voluntary family planning
Still have the world's highest fertility rates
Used stricter penalties than China
Abandoned family planning entirely

subtopics.title: The Stadium That Fills in the Last Minute

questions.question: In the 24-hour stadium picture of population history, the first billion people are seated:
options: In the first hour
Only by about quarter to midnight — after nearly the whole day
By midday
In the final minute

questions.question: The population explosion happened because:
options: People suddenly started having more babies than ever before
Stadiums were built larger
Migration increased between countries
Death slowed down — deaths collapsed while births carried on as before for a generation or two

questions.question: The queue outside the stadium getting shorter every year represents:
options: Rising death rates worldwide
The end of the census
The falling growth rate, as families everywhere shrink
Fewer stadiums being built

subtopics.title: Too Many for What? The Lifeboat Question

questions.question: In the lifeboat picture, the boat's rating for 20 people represents:
options: The carrying capacity — the number the resources can support decently
The population density
The birth rate
The number of people currently aboard

questions.question: Crowded is not the same as overloaded means:
options: Density and overpopulation are identical measures
A dense place with strong resources can be fine, while a sparse place with weak resources can be overpopulated
Only cities can be overpopulated
Deserts can never be overpopulated

questions.question: A region becoming overpopulated without a single person being added happens when:
options: The census is recounted
The birth rate rises
Young people return from the cities
The resource base shrinks — through drought, erosion or exhausted wells — so the boat gets smaller beneath the same crowd

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of strain from overpopulation named in the lesson?
options: Falling school enrolment as classrooms empty
Family plots splitting smaller each generation while settlements outgrow pipes and power lines
Rising wages from labour shortages
Underused clinics and hospitals

questions.question: The chain from the school gate to the birth rate runs:
options: Girls finish school, marry later, gain plans and incomes, invest in fewer children's schooling, and use family planning
Schools directly limit family sizes by law
Educated women always remain unmarried
School fees make children profitable

questions.question: Save more babies slows growth because:
options: Clinics register births more slowly
It lowers the death rate, which is the same as lowering the birth rate
When child survival becomes normal, parents stop having extra children as insurance
Saved babies emigrate when they grow up

questions.question: Pensions reduce birth rates because:
options: Pensioners cannot raise children
Pension paperwork discourages marriage
Pensions are only paid to small families
Where old age is protected by a pension, children are no longer a retirement plan

questions.question: South Africa's fertility fell from about six children per woman to about 2,3 through:
options: A legal limit on family size
Education, urbanisation, clinic-based family planning and choice — never compulsion
Mass emigration of young families
A rise in infant mortality
